transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm happy to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling after your surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery or anything that's been concerning you?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Thanks for taking my call. I'm feeling alright, but I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as watering plants or light pruning, about 1 week after your surgery. However, it's best to avoid any heavy lifting or bending for a month. Also, make sure to wear protective eyewear when gardening to shield your eyes from any debris or dust. Does that sound okay to you? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That sounds manageable, thanks for the advice! I do have another question — when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should have started using preservative-free eye drops four times a day as soon as you got home from the hospital. If you're running out, you can ask your GP for more. They can help you get a refill. Do you have any other questions about your eye drops or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, I'll make sure to do that. My next question is about sensitivity to bright light. I'm very sensitive to it right now—is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. But if it's severe or you're also experiencing redness and pain, we'd like to check it out further. If it's just mild and you're finding it brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. Does that make sense? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That does make sense, thank you. I have one more question—should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's all for now. Thanks for answering my questions, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions about your cataract surgery recovery. Now, I just want to check in with you: do you feel like all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I feel much better informed now. Thanks again for your help!

verdict.label: pass
